questions.q: What does the If/Else branch on contractor_type decide in this flow?
options: Whether the flow should run at all that day
Which access-revocation handling applies, since IT contractors typically have accounts in more systems than non-IT contractors
Which manager receives the approval request
Whether the trigger is Record-based or Scheduled
questions.explain: The branch exists because IT and non-IT contractors genuinely need different revocation handling downstream — the same test Lesson 6 used for when a branch earns its place.

questions.q: What does the calling flow pass into the Revoke Access subflow as its Input, and what does the subflow return as its Output?
options: Input: the manager's approval decision; Output: the contractor's end date
Input: nothing; Output: a new flow trigger
Input: the IT task record; Output: the contractor_type field
Input: the contractor's sys_user record; Output: a revocation status such as success or failed-with-reason
questions.explain: The subflow is built around a defined Input (the user record) and Output (a status), the exact pattern Lesson 14 taught for subflow inputs and outputs.

questions.q: Why does building Revoke Access as a subflow matter beyond just keeping this one flow tidy?
options: Subflows run faster than inline flow logic in every case
A subflow is required whenever an If/Else branch is present
The same subflow could later be called from an entirely different flow, such as a security-incident flow, without rebuilding the revocation logic
Subflows cannot return any output, so tidiness is the only benefit
questions.explain: Reusability across entirely different flows is the real payoff Lesson 13 argued for choosing a subflow over inline logic in the first place.

questions.q: Why does the manager's Approval action for equipment return run regardless of the subflow's exact revocation outcome?
options: The approval step automatically cancels if the subflow fails
Approvals cannot be placed after a Call Subflow step
Equipment return is only relevant for IT contractors
Equipment return is a separate concern from system access, so a flow condition on the subflow's output only decides whether to also flag a security follow-up
questions.explain: The flow treats equipment return and access revocation as independent concerns, checking the subflow's output only to decide on an additional security flag.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the final Create Record action that assigns a task to the IT queue?
options: It deletes the contractor record once access is revoked
It turns the flow's outcome into a concrete, assigned record a human can act on, since automation alone can't fully close out the process
It replaces the need for the manager's approval
It re-triggers the scheduled trigger for the next day
questions.explain: The Create Record action gives IT something concrete and assigned to act on, summarizing what the flow did and what still needs attention.
